description: Composite EBSD figure (Fig. 5) for the Fe-Mn-Al-Cu 17Al alloy, organised as three rows × two columns of paired inverse pole figure (IPF) orientation maps and phase maps. All panels share an IPF colour key labelled 001 (top), 101 (lower-left) and 111 (lower-right), and a phase legend reading BCC (red), α-Mn (blue), β-Mn (green) and FCC (pink). Row (a): 525 °C/10 h; (a1) has a 200 µm scale bar and shows red BCC α grains bounded by a green β-Mn network along grain boundaries, while the magnified (a2) (5 µm) carries arrows labelling residual α and small α-Mn particles. Row (b): 575 °C/6 h; (b1) (100 µm) is an equiaxed, randomly oriented multicoloured grain structure whose phase map is almost entirely green β-Mn, while (b2) (2 µm) labels magenta "New FCC phase" particles inside β-Mn. Row (c): 650 °C/10 h; (c1) (200 µm) is again a fully equiaxed grain structure with an almost pure β-Mn phase map, and (c2) (5 µm) labels "New BCC phase" particles within β-Mn. The figure demonstrates that the α matrix progressively transforms to β-Mn with increasing aging temperature/time, and that new BCC and FCC precipitates appear within the β-Mn at the higher temperatures. No composition or phase-fraction values are printed on the panels.

observations.observation: All phase maps in the figure use the same legend: BCC (red), α-Mn (blue), β-Mn (green), FCC (pink).
The IPF colour key present in every IPF map is a stereographic triangle labelled 001 at the top, 101 at the lower left and 111 at the lower right.
Printed scale bars are 200 µm in (a1) and (c1), 100 µm in (b1), 5 µm in (a2) and (c2), and 2 µm in (b2).
In the (a1) phase map the red BCC α matrix dominates and green β-Mn forms a connected network along the α grain boundaries, i.e. only a minor β-Mn fraction after 525 °C/10 h.
In (a2) arrows point to red regions labelled 'α' and to small particles labelled 'α-Mn', consistent with residual α matrix plus α-Mn inside the α grains.

The (b1) inverse pole figure map shows equiaxed, randomly oriented grains of many colours while its accompanying phase map is almost entirely green β-Mn, indicating near-complete transformation of the α matrix after 575 °C/6 h.
In (b2) arrows label magenta particles as 'New FCC phase' dispersed inside the green β-Mn field.
In (c2) arrows label small particles within the green β-Mn as 'New BCC phase' after aging at 650 °C for 10 h.
The (c1) phase map is uniformly green β-Mn with no visible red BCC matrix, matching the near-complete α-to-β-Mn transformation seen in (b1).

The caption states the figure shows EBSD inverse pole figures and phase maps of the 17Al alloy after aging at (a) 525 °C for 10 h, (b) 575 °C for 6 h and (c) 650 °C for 10 h, with (a2-c2) being magnified views of (a-c).

The citing text states that after aging the 17Al alloy at 525 °C for 10 h only a small amount of β-Mn (20.5 %) formed along the α grain boundaries and within the α grains, with some small α-Mn particles in the α matrix.

The citing text states that in samples aged at 575 °C for 6 h and 650 °C for 10 h the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn, with a small amount of new precipitates of BCC (red highlighted) and FCC (pink highlighted) structure within the β-Mn.

The citing text states that the EBSD results in Fig. 5, together with Figs. 4 and 6, clearly revealed the presence of the BCC phase within the β-Mn, and that the content of the FCC Cu-rich phase between β-Mn interfaces decreases with increasing Al content.

subfigures.description: Lower-magnification pair for 525 °C/10 h: left is an IPF map (001/101/111 colour triangle) dominated by green and yellow/red regions; right is the phase map, dominated by red BCC α with a green β-Mn (and minor blue α-Mn) network decorating the α grain boundaries. 200 µm scale bars on both images.

Magnified view of (a). Left IPF map shows banded red/yellow and green regions; right phase map (5 µm scale bar) shows large green β-Mn regions interleaved with red BCC, with arrows labelling 'α' (red) and 'α-Mn' (small particles).

Pair for 575 °C/6 h at 100 µm scale. IPF map shows equiaxed, randomly oriented grains in many colours (blue, purple, pink, green, red); the phase map is essentially uniform green, i.e. β-Mn, with only rare isolated specks.

Magnified view of (b) at 2 µm scale. IPF map is mostly pink/violet; the phase map is green β-Mn containing scattered magenta particles, with three arrows labelling 'New FCC phase' and a text label 'β-Mn' on the green field.
Pair for 650 °C/10 h at 200 µm scale. IPF map shows coarse equiaxed grains in many orientations; the phase map is uniformly green β-Mn with essentially no red BCC or blue α-Mn visible.
Magnified view of (c) at 5 µm scale. IPF map is predominantly pale green/yellow; the phase map is green β-Mn with multiple small scattered particles, arrows labelling 'New BCC phase' within the β-Mn.

unreadable_items: panel (c2): the exact colour of the particles marked 'New BCC phase' is hard to resolve at the supplied resolution; the legend assigns BCC to red, whereas the highlighted particles look pinkish/dark
